html:
Fourah Bay College is a college in Freetown, Sierra Leone, founded in 1827. It was the first Western-style university college in West Africa.

The Church Missionary Society set it up to train teachers and clergy among the freed Africans who had been landed at Freetown from slave ships. Its first student was Samuel Ajayi Crowther, who became the first African Anglican bishop.

From 1876 it was linked to Durham University in England and could give degrees. Students came from all over British West Africa, and its graduates became clergy, teachers, lawyers, doctors and civil servants. This earned Freetown the name "the Athens of West Africa". Many of the first generation of West African nationalists studied there or were taught by its graduates.

It became part of the University of Sierra Leone in 1967. The college suffered badly in the civil war of the 1990s but has since reopened.
sum: Fourah Bay College is a college in Freetown, Sierra Leone, founded in 1827. It was the first Western-style university college in West Africa.
